title: Rows of a Rademacher matrix are mutually independent
statement: Equip the space of $k \times d$ real arrays $\omega = (\omega_{ij})$ with the joint Rademacher product measure, under which the $k \cdot d$ entries are independent and each $\omega_{ij}$ takes the values $-1$ and $+1$ with equal probability $1/2$. For each index $i \in \{1,\dots,k\}$, let $R_i$ be the $i$-th row, that is, the $\mathbb{R}^d$-valued random variable $\omega \mapsto (\omega_{ij})_{j}$. Then the family $(R_i)_{i}$ of $k$ rows is mutually independent.
hypotheses_covered: sample space is k×d real arrays
measure is the joint Rademacher product measure (entries independent, each ±1 with probability 1/2)
each random variable is the i-th row map ω ↦ (ω_{ij})_j, valued in ℝ^d
conclusion: the family of k rows is mutually independent
replaced:
The $k$ row vectors $i \mapsto (\omega_{ij})_{j}$, viewed as
$\mathrm{Fin}\,d \to \mathbb{R}$-valued random variables, are mutually
independent under the joint measure.
